report.title: United States v. Google LLC: where the search case stands

paragraphs.text: The case is on appeal. The district court found in August 2024 that Google unlawfully maintained its search monopoly, ordered behavioural remedies in September 2025 and entered its Final Judgment on 5 December 2025. Google appealed to the D.C. Circuit on 16 January 2026, and the United States appealed on 3 February 2026.
Meanwhile the district court is supervising compliance: the United States filed its second status report on Google's compliance with the Final Judgment on 17 September 2026.

The Justice Department and eleven states sued on 20 October 2020, alleging that Google unlawfully maintained monopolies in search and search advertising through anticompetitive and exclusionary practices.
In August 2024 Judge Amit Mehta ruled against Google. Google said at the time that it would appeal, arguing that the court had recognised it offers the best search engine.

The remedies decision of 2 September 2025 barred exclusive contracts for distributing Search, Chrome, Google Assistant and the Gemini app, and required Google to share certain search data with, and offer syndication to, some competitors. TechCrunch reported that the court did not order a break-up such as a sale of Chrome.

After the Final Judgment, both sides appealed. Alphabet's latest quarterly filing reports that the court denied Google's request to pause certain remedies as premature, and that state attorneys general also appealed.
The D.C. Circuit could uphold, narrow or widen the remedies, and its decision could itself be appealed. Until then the Final Judgment's requirements apply as the district court supervises them.
